console_report: The maintainer reports recurring drops after returning to the 120 FPS limit. The current session was retrieved through Cyberduck and identifies build 284, Fabric 26.3, render and simulation distance 12, Sodium 0.9.3-beta.1 and Vitrail 0.13.0-beta, with no shader pack selected. The transition toward roughly two seconds per 240 frames is consistent with the reported cap change.
frame_evidence: The capture contains 49 overlapping frame summaries and 16 late-frame stacks. In the windows ending from JVM uptime 70720 ms onward, the maximum was 71.050 ms, with later 61.133 and 56.898 ms maxima. Some 240-frame windows were close to 2000 ms. The totals describe frame intervals in Minecraft, without measuring physical scanout.
stack_evidence: Early traces include Sodium's mapped staging buffer flip and Minecraft's Vulkan submit completion path for vertex buffer recycling. The later traces include client lighting, feature rendering, Vulkan command recording and HUD extraction. Vitrail hooks appear in some later traces despite no selected pack. Each trace is a single snapshot inside an over-budget frame and cannot establish that the sampled method consumed the excess time.
gc_evidence: No allocation stall appears in the collected 284 GC log. The largest reported JVM safepoint was 4.463 ms, and the largest in the two windows with the 71.050 ms frame was 1.123 ms.
next_console_check: Reproduce at 120 FPS with only Vitrail disabled, keeping Sodium, other mods, the same route and both distances fixed. Collect matched frame and stack reports. This isolates the render hooks still active with shader packs off before changing native synchronization or default settings.
